item.title: Drill 2026-10-22: reverse (signed divide by 8)
item.description:
Reverse a short function (Windows x64)
Target: Windows x86-64 (first arg in `ecx`; return in `eax`).
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: mov eax, ecx cdq and edx, 7 add eax, edx sar eax, 3 ret ```
What does `mystery(-9)` return, and why not just a bare `sar eax, 3`?
ANSWER:
```c int mystery(int x) { return x / 8; } ```
`mystery(-9)` returns `-1` (a bare `sar` would give `-2`).
- `cdq` copies the sign bit of `eax` into all of `edx` (0 or -1); `and edx, 7` turns that into a bias of 0 (x >= 0) or 7 (x < 0). - `sar` alone rounds toward negative infinity (floor), but C division truncates toward zero; adding 2^n - 1 to negatives first fixes this: (-9 + 7) >> 3 = -1. - Signed divide by a power of two compiles to this bias + `sar` instead of a slow `idiv`; an unsigned divide would just be `shr`.
